symbols.name: inline_schema
symbols.description:
Whether JSON Schemas generated for this type should be included directly in parent schemas,
rather than being re-used where possible using the `$ref` keyword.

For trivial types (such as primitives), this should return `true`. For more complex types,
it should return `false`. For recursive types, this **must** return `false` to prevent
infinite cycles when generating schemas.

By default, this returns `false`.

symbols.name: json_schema
symbols.description:
Generates a JSON Schema for this type.

If the returned schema depends on any [non-inlined](JsonSchema::inline_schema)
schemas, then this method will add them to the [`SchemaGenerator`]'s schema definitions.

This should not return a `$ref` schema.

[`SchemaGenerator`]: https://docs.rs/schemars/1.2.3/schemars/generate/struct.SchemaGenerator.html

symbols.name: schema_id
symbols.description:
Returns a string that uniquely identifies the schema produced by this type.

symbols.name: inline_schema
symbols.description:
Whether JSON Schemas generated for this type should be included directly in parent schemas,
rather than being re-used where possible using the `$ref` keyword.

For trivial types (such as primitives), this should return `true`. For more complex types,
it should return `false`. For recursive types, this **must** return `false` to prevent
infinite cycles when generating schemas.

By default, this returns `false`.

symbols.name: json_schema
symbols.description:
Generates a JSON Schema for this type.

If the returned schema depends on any [non-inlined](JsonSchema::inline_schema)
schemas, then this method will add them to the [`SchemaGenerator`]'s schema definitions.

This should not return a `$ref` schema.

[`SchemaGenerator`]: https://docs.rs/schemars/1.2.3/schemars/generate/struct.SchemaGenerator.html

symbols.name: schema_id
symbols.description:
Returns a string that uniquely identifies the schema produced by this type.

This does not have to be a human-readable string, and the value will not itself be included
in generated schemas. If two types produce different schemas, then they **must** have
different `schema_id()`s, but two types that produce identical schemas should *ideally*
have the same `schema_id()`.

The default implementation returns the same value as
[`schema_name()`](JsonSchema::schema_name).

symbols.name: schema_name
symbols.description:
The name of the generated JSON Schema.

This is used as the title for root schemas, and the key within the root's `definitions`
property for subschemas.

symbols.name: deref
symbols.description:
Dereferences the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be mutably dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref_mut`] concurrently.

symbols.name: deref_mut
symbols.declaration: unsafe fn deref_mut<'a>(ptr: usize) -> &'a mut T;
symbols.description:
Mutably dereferences the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref`] or [`Pointable::deref_mut`]
  concurrently.

symbols.name: drop
symbols.description:
Drops the object pointed to by the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref`] or [`Pointable::deref_mut`]
  concurrently.

inline_schema
symbols.description:
Whether JSON Schemas generated for this type should be included directly in parent schemas,
rather than being re-used where possible using the `$ref` keyword.

For trivial types (such as primitives), this should return `true`. For more complex types,
it should return `false`. For recursive types, this **must** return `false` to prevent
infinite cycles when generating schemas.

By default, this returns `false`.

symbols.name: json_schema
symbols.description:
Generates a JSON Schema for this type.

If the returned schema depends on any [non-inlined](JsonSchema::inline_schema)
schemas, then this method will add them to the [`SchemaGenerator`]'s schema definitions.

This should not return a `$ref` schema.

[`SchemaGenerator`]: https://docs.rs/schemars/1.2.3/schemars/generate/struct.SchemaGenerator.html

symbols.name: schema_id
symbols.description:
Returns a string that uniquely identifies the schema produced by this type.

This does not have to be a human-readable string, and the value will not itself be included
in generated schemas. If two types produce different schemas, then they **must** have
different `schema_id()`s, but two types that produce identical schemas should *ideally*
have the same `schema_id()`.

The default implementation returns the same value as
[`schema_name()`](JsonSchema::schema_name).

symbols.name: schema_name
symbols.description:
The name of the generated JSON Schema.

This is used as the title for root schemas, and the key within the root's `definitions`
property for subschemas.

- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be mutably dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref_mut`] concurrently.

inline_schema
symbols.description:
Whether JSON Schemas generated for this type should be included directly in parent schemas,
rather than being re-used where possible using the `$ref` keyword.

For trivial types (such as primitives), this should return `true`. For more complex types,
it should return `false`. For recursive types, this **must** return `false` to prevent
infinite cycles when generating schemas.

By default, this returns `false`.

symbols.name: json_schema
symbols.description:
Generates a JSON Schema for this type.

If the returned schema depends on any [non-inlined](JsonSchema::inline_schema)
schemas, then this method will add them to the [`SchemaGenerator`]'s schema definitions.

This should not return a `$ref` schema.

[`SchemaGenerator`]: https://docs.rs/schemars/1.2.3/schemars/generate/struct.SchemaGenerator.html

symbols.name: schema_id
symbols.description:
Returns a string that uniquely identifies the schema produced by this type.

This does not have to be a human-readable string, and the value will not itself be included
in generated schemas. If two types produce different schemas, then they **must** have
different `schema_id()`s, but two types that produce identical schemas should *ideally*
have the same `schema_id()`.

The default implementation returns the same value as
[`schema_name()`](JsonSchema::schema_name).

symbols.name: schema_name
symbols.description:
The name of the generated JSON Schema.

This is used as the title for root schemas, and the key within the root's `definitions`
property for subschemas.

symbols.name: deref
symbols.description:
Dereferences the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be mutably dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref_mut`] concurrently.

symbols.name: deref_mut
symbols.declaration: unsafe fn deref_mut<'a>(ptr: usize) -> &'a mut T;
symbols.description:
Mutably dereferences the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref`] or [`Pointable::deref_mut`]
  concurrently.

symbols.name: drop
symbols.description:
Drops the object pointed to by the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref`] or [`Pointable::deref_mut`]
  concurrently.

symbols.name: init
symbols.declaration: unsafe fn init(init: <T as Pointable>::Init) -> usize;
symbols.description:
Initializes a with the given initializer.

# Safety

The result should be a multiple of `ALIGN`.

symbols.id: rust:refquill:function:refquill::model::Kind::impl<T> ToOwned for T where T: Clone::to_owned
symbols.name: to_owned
inline_schema
symbols.description:
Whether JSON Schemas generated for this type should be included directly in parent schemas,
rather than being re-used where possible using the `$ref` keyword.

For trivial types (such as primitives), this should return `true`. For more complex types,
it should return `false`. For recursive types, this **must** return `false` to prevent
infinite cycles when generating schemas.

By default, this returns `false`.

symbols.name: json_schema
symbols.description:
Generates a JSON Schema for this type.

If the returned schema depends on any [non-inlined](JsonSchema::inline_schema)
schemas, then this method will add them to the [`SchemaGenerator`]'s schema definitions.

This should not return a `$ref` schema.

[`SchemaGenerator`]: https://docs.rs/schemars/1.2.3/schemars/generate/struct.SchemaGenerator.html

symbols.name: schema_id
symbols.description:
Returns a string that uniquely identifies the schema produced by this type.

This does not have to be a human-readable string, and the value will not itself be included
in generated schemas. If two types produce different schemas, then they **must** have
different `schema_id()`s, but two types that produce identical schemas should *ideally*
have the same `schema_id()`.

The default implementation returns the same value as
[`schema_name()`](JsonSchema::schema_name).

symbols.name: schema_name
symbols.description:
The name of the generated JSON Schema.

This is used as the title for root schemas, and the key within the root's `definitions`
property for subschemas.

deserialize

manual for more information about how to implement this method.

[impl-deserialize]: https://serde.rs/impl-deserialize.html

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be mutably dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref_mut`] concurrently.

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].

  concurrently.

symbols.name: drop

symbols.id: rust:refquill:function:refquill::model::Language::impl<T> ToOwned for T where T: Clone::to_owned
symbols.name: to_owned
inline_schema
symbols.description:
Whether JSON Schemas generated for this type should be included directly in parent schemas,
rather than being re-used where possible using the `$ref` keyword.

For trivial types (such as primitives), this should return `true`. For more complex types,
it should return `false`. For recursive types, this **must** return `false` to prevent
infinite cycles when generating schemas.

By default, this returns `false`.

symbols.name: json_schema
symbols.description:
Generates a JSON Schema for this type.

If the returned schema depends on any [non-inlined](JsonSchema::inline_schema)
schemas, then this method will add them to the [`SchemaGenerator`]'s schema definitions.

This should not return a `$ref` schema.

[`SchemaGenerator`]: https://docs.rs/schemars/1.2.3/schemars/generate/struct.SchemaGenerator.html

symbols.name: schema_id
symbols.description:
Returns a string that uniquely identifies the schema produced by this type.

This does not have to be a human-readable string, and the value will not itself be included
in generated schemas. If two types produce different schemas, then they **must** have
different `schema_id()`s, but two types that produce identical schemas should *ideally*
have the same `schema_id()`.

The default implementation returns the same value as
[`schema_name()`](JsonSchema::schema_name).

symbols.name: schema_name
symbols.description:
The name of the generated JSON Schema.

This is used as the title for root schemas, and the key within the root's `definitions`
property for subschemas.

symbols.name: deref
symbols.description:
Dereferences the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be mutably dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref_mut`] concurrently.

symbols.name: deref_mut
symbols.declaration: unsafe fn deref_mut<'a>(ptr: usize) -> &'a mut T;
symbols.description:
Mutably dereferences the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref`] or [`Pointable::deref_mut`]
  concurrently.

symbols.name: drop
symbols.description:
Drops the object pointed to by the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref`] or [`Pointable::deref_mut`]
  concurrently.

symbols.declaration: unsafe fn init(init: <T as Pointable>::Init) -> usize;
symbols.description:

symbols.name: to_owned
inline_schema
symbols.description:
Whether JSON Schemas generated for this type should be included directly in parent schemas,
rather than being re-used where possible using the `$ref` keyword.

For trivial types (such as primitives), this should return `true`. For more complex types,
it should return `false`. For recursive types, this **must** return `false` to prevent
infinite cycles when generating schemas.

By default, this returns `false`.

symbols.name: json_schema
symbols.description:
Generates a JSON Schema for this type.

If the returned schema depends on any [non-inlined](JsonSchema::inline_schema)
schemas, then this method will add them to the [`SchemaGenerator`]'s schema definitions.

This should not return a `$ref` schema.

[`SchemaGenerator`]: https://docs.rs/schemars/1.2.3/schemars/generate/struct.SchemaGenerator.html

symbols.name: schema_id
symbols.description:
Returns a string that uniquely identifies the schema produced by this type.

This does not have to be a human-readable string, and the value will not itself be included
in generated schemas. If two types produce different schemas, then they **must** have
different `schema_id()`s, but two types that produce identical schemas should *ideally*
have the same `schema_id()`.

The default implementation returns the same value as
[`schema_name()`](JsonSchema::schema_name).

symbols.name: schema_name
symbols.description:
The name of the generated JSON Schema.

This is used as the title for root schemas, and the key within the root's `definitions`
property for subschemas.

deserialize

inline_schema
symbols.description:
Whether JSON Schemas generated for this type should be included directly in parent schemas,
rather than being re-used where possible using the `$ref` keyword.

For trivial types (such as primitives), this should return `true`. For more complex types,
it should return `false`. For recursive types, this **must** return `false` to prevent
infinite cycles when generating schemas.

By default, this returns `false`.

symbols.name: json_schema
symbols.description:
Generates a JSON Schema for this type.

If the returned schema depends on any [non-inlined](JsonSchema::inline_schema)
schemas, then this method will add them to the [`SchemaGenerator`]'s schema definitions.

This should not return a `$ref` schema.

[`SchemaGenerator`]: https://docs.rs/schemars/1.2.3/schemars/generate/struct.SchemaGenerator.html

symbols.name: schema_id
symbols.description:
Returns a string that uniquely identifies the schema produced by this type.

This does not have to be a human-readable string, and the value will not itself be included
in generated schemas. If two types produce different schemas, then they **must** have
different `schema_id()`s, but two types that produce identical schemas should *ideally*
have the same `schema_id()`.

The default implementation returns the same value as
[`schema_name()`](JsonSchema::schema_name).

symbols.name: schema_name
symbols.description:
The name of the generated JSON Schema.

This is used as the title for root schemas, and the key within the root's `definitions`
property for subschemas.

symbols.name: deref
symbols.description:
Dereferences the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be mutably dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref_mut`] concurrently.

symbols.name: deref_mut
symbols.declaration: unsafe fn deref_mut<'a>(ptr: usize) -> &'a mut T;
symbols.description:
Mutably dereferences the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref`] or [`Pointable::deref_mut`]
  concurrently.

symbols.name: drop
symbols.description:
Drops the object pointed to by the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref`] or [`Pointable::deref_mut`]
  concurrently.

symbols.name: init
symbols.declaration: unsafe fn init(init: <T as Pointable>::Init) -> usize;
symbols.description:
Initializes a with the given initializer.

symbols.name: to_owned
inline_schema
symbols.description:
Whether JSON Schemas generated for this type should be included directly in parent schemas,
rather than being re-used where possible using the `$ref` keyword.

For trivial types (such as primitives), this should return `true`. For more complex types,
it should return `false`. For recursive types, this **must** return `false` to prevent
infinite cycles when generating schemas.

By default, this returns `false`.

symbols.name: json_schema
symbols.description:
Generates a JSON Schema for this type.

If the returned schema depends on any [non-inlined](JsonSchema::inline_schema)
schemas, then this method will add them to the [`SchemaGenerator`]'s schema definitions.

This should not return a `$ref` schema.

[`SchemaGenerator`]: https://docs.rs/schemars/1.2.3/schemars/generate/struct.SchemaGenerator.html

symbols.name: schema_id
symbols.description:
Returns a string that uniquely identifies the schema produced by this type.

This does not have to be a human-readable string, and the value will not itself be included
in generated schemas. If two types produce different schemas, then they **must** have
different `schema_id()`s, but two types that produce identical schemas should *ideally*
have the same `schema_id()`.

The default implementation returns the same value as
[`schema_name()`](JsonSchema::schema_name).

symbols.name: schema_name
symbols.description:
The name of the generated JSON Schema.

This is used as the title for root schemas, and the key within the root's `definitions`
property for subschemas.

deserialize

manual for more information about how to implement this method.

[impl-deserialize]: https://serde.rs/impl-deserialize.html

inline_schema
symbols.description:
Whether JSON Schemas generated for this type should be included directly in parent schemas,
rather than being re-used where possible using the `$ref` keyword.

For trivial types (such as primitives), this should return `true`. For more complex types,
it should return `false`. For recursive types, this **must** return `false` to prevent
infinite cycles when generating schemas.

By default, this returns `false`.

symbols.name: json_schema
symbols.description:
Generates a JSON Schema for this type.

If the returned schema depends on any [non-inlined](JsonSchema::inline_schema)
schemas, then this method will add them to the [`SchemaGenerator`]'s schema definitions.

This should not return a `$ref` schema.

[`SchemaGenerator`]: https://docs.rs/schemars/1.2.3/schemars/generate/struct.SchemaGenerator.html

symbols.name: schema_id
symbols.description:
Returns a string that uniquely identifies the schema produced by this type.

This does not have to be a human-readable string, and the value will not itself be included
in generated schemas. If two types produce different schemas, then they **must** have
different `schema_id()`s, but two types that produce identical schemas should *ideally*
have the same `schema_id()`.

The default implementation returns the same value as
[`schema_name()`](JsonSchema::schema_name).

symbols.name: schema_name
symbols.description:
The name of the generated JSON Schema.

This is used as the title for root schemas, and the key within the root's `definitions`
property for subschemas.

symbols.name: deref
symbols.description:
Dereferences the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be mutably dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref_mut`] concurrently.

symbols.name: deref_mut
symbols.declaration: unsafe fn deref_mut<'a>(ptr: usize) -> &'a mut T;
symbols.description:
Mutably dereferences the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref`] or [`Pointable::deref_mut`]
  concurrently.

symbols.name: drop
symbols.description:
Drops the object pointed to by the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref`] or [`Pointable::deref_mut`]
  concurrently.

symbols.name: init
symbols.declaration: unsafe fn init(init: <T as Pointable>::Init) -> usize;
symbols.description:
Initializes a with the given initializer.

# Safety

The result should be a multiple of `ALIGN`.

symbols.name: to_owned
inline_schema
symbols.description:
Whether JSON Schemas generated for this type should be included directly in parent schemas,
rather than being re-used where possible using the `$ref` keyword.

For trivial types (such as primitives), this should return `true`. For more complex types,
it should return `false`. For recursive types, this **must** return `false` to prevent
infinite cycles when generating schemas.

By default, this returns `false`.

symbols.name: json_schema
symbols.description:
Generates a JSON Schema for this type.

If the returned schema depends on any [non-inlined](JsonSchema::inline_schema)
schemas, then this method will add them to the [`SchemaGenerator`]'s schema definitions.

This should not return a `$ref` schema.

[`SchemaGenerator`]: https://docs.rs/schemars/1.2.3/schemars/generate/struct.SchemaGenerator.html

symbols.name: schema_id
symbols.description:
Returns a string that uniquely identifies the schema produced by this type.

This does not have to be a human-readable string, and the value will not itself be included
in generated schemas. If two types produce different schemas, then they **must** have
different `schema_id()`s, but two types that produce identical schemas should *ideally*
have the same `schema_id()`.

The default implementation returns the same value as
[`schema_name()`](JsonSchema::schema_name).

symbols.name: schema_name
symbols.description:
The name of the generated JSON Schema.

This is used as the title for root schemas, and the key within the root's `definitions`
property for subschemas.

symbols.name: serialize
deserialize
symbols.description:
Deserialize this value from the given Serde deserializer.

See the [Implementing `Deserialize`][impl-deserialize] section of the
manual for more information about how to implement this method.

[impl-deserialize]: https://serde.rs/impl-deserialize.html

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be mutably dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref_mut`] concurrently.

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].

  concurrently.

symbols.name: drop

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].

symbols.name: to_owned
inline_schema
symbols.description:
Whether JSON Schemas generated for this type should be included directly in parent schemas,
rather than being re-used where possible using the `$ref` keyword.

For trivial types (such as primitives), this should return `true`. For more complex types,
it should return `false`. For recursive types, this **must** return `false` to prevent
infinite cycles when generating schemas.

By default, this returns `false`.

symbols.name: json_schema
symbols.description:
Generates a JSON Schema for this type.

If the returned schema depends on any [non-inlined](JsonSchema::inline_schema)
schemas, then this method will add them to the [`SchemaGenerator`]'s schema definitions.

This should not return a `$ref` schema.

[`SchemaGenerator`]: https://docs.rs/schemars/1.2.3/schemars/generate/struct.SchemaGenerator.html

symbols.name: schema_id
symbols.description:
Returns a string that uniquely identifies the schema produced by this type.

This does not have to be a human-readable string, and the value will not itself be included
in generated schemas. If two types produce different schemas, then they **must** have
different `schema_id()`s, but two types that produce identical schemas should *ideally*
have the same `schema_id()`.

The default implementation returns the same value as
[`schema_name()`](JsonSchema::schema_name).

symbols.name: schema_name
symbols.description:
The name of the generated JSON Schema.

This is used as the title for root schemas, and the key within the root's `definitions`
property for subschemas.

symbols.name: deref
symbols.description:
Dereferences the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be mutably dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref_mut`] concurrently.

symbols.name: deref_mut
symbols.declaration: unsafe fn deref_mut<'a>(ptr: usize) -> &'a mut T;
symbols.description:
Mutably dereferences the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref`] or [`Pointable::deref_mut`]
  concurrently.

symbols.name: drop
symbols.description:
Drops the object pointed to by the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref`] or [`Pointable::deref_mut`]
  concurrently.

symbols.name: init
symbols.declaration: unsafe fn init(init: <T as Pointable>::Init) -> usize;
symbols.description:
Initializes a with the given initializer.

# Safety

The result should be a multiple of `ALIGN`.

symbols.name: inline_schema
symbols.description:
Whether JSON Schemas generated for this type should be included directly in parent schemas,
rather than being re-used where possible using the `$ref` keyword.

For trivial types (such as primitives), this should return `true`. For more complex types,
it should return `false`. For recursive types, this **must** return `false` to prevent
infinite cycles when generating schemas.

By default, this returns `false`.

symbols.name: json_schema
symbols.description:
Generates a JSON Schema for this type.

If the returned schema depends on any [non-inlined](JsonSchema::inline_schema)
schemas, then this method will add them to the [`SchemaGenerator`]'s schema definitions.

This should not return a `$ref` schema.

[`SchemaGenerator`]: https://docs.rs/schemars/1.2.3/schemars/generate/struct.SchemaGenerator.html

symbols.name: schema_id
symbols.description:
Returns a string that uniquely identifies the schema produced by this type.

This does not have to be a human-readable string, and the value will not itself be included
in generated schemas. If two types produce different schemas, then they **must** have
different `schema_id()`s, but two types that produce identical schemas should *ideally*
have the same `schema_id()`.

The default implementation returns the same value as
[`schema_name()`](JsonSchema::schema_name).

symbols.name: schema_name
symbols.description:
The name of the generated JSON Schema.

This is used as the title for root schemas, and the key within the root's `definitions`
property for subschemas.

symbols.name: inline_schema
symbols.description:
Whether JSON Schemas generated for this type should be included directly in parent schemas,
rather than being re-used where possible using the `$ref` keyword.

For trivial types (such as primitives), this should return `true`. For more complex types,
it should return `false`. For recursive types, this **must** return `false` to prevent
infinite cycles when generating schemas.

By default, this returns `false`.

symbols.name: json_schema
symbols.description:
Generates a JSON Schema for this type.

If the returned schema depends on any [non-inlined](JsonSchema::inline_schema)
schemas, then this method will add them to the [`SchemaGenerator`]'s schema definitions.

This should not return a `$ref` schema.

[`SchemaGenerator`]: https://docs.rs/schemars/1.2.3/schemars/generate/struct.SchemaGenerator.html

symbols.name: schema_id
symbols.description:
Returns a string that uniquely identifies the schema produced by this type.

This does not have to be a human-readable string, and the value will not itself be included
in generated schemas. If two types produce different schemas, then they **must** have
different `schema_id()`s, but two types that produce identical schemas should *ideally*
have the same `schema_id()`.

The default implementation returns the same value as
[`schema_name()`](JsonSchema::schema_name).

symbols.name: schema_name
symbols.description:
The name of the generated JSON Schema.

This is used as the title for root schemas, and the key within the root's `definitions`
property for subschemas.

symbols.name: inline_schema
symbols.description:
Whether JSON Schemas generated for this type should be included directly in parent schemas,
rather than being re-used where possible using the `$ref` keyword.

For trivial types (such as primitives), this should return `true`. For more complex types,
it should return `false`. For recursive types, this **must** return `false` to prevent
infinite cycles when generating schemas.

By default, this returns `false`.

symbols.name: json_schema
symbols.description:
Generates a JSON Schema for this type.

If the returned schema depends on any [non-inlined](JsonSchema::inline_schema)
schemas, then this method will add them to the [`SchemaGenerator`]'s schema definitions.

This should not return a `$ref` schema.

[`SchemaGenerator`]: https://docs.rs/schemars/1.2.3/schemars/generate/struct.SchemaGenerator.html

symbols.name: schema_id
symbols.description:
Returns a string that uniquely identifies the schema produced by this type.

This does not have to be a human-readable string, and the value will not itself be included
in generated schemas. If two types produce different schemas, then they **must** have
different `schema_id()`s, but two types that produce identical schemas should *ideally*
have the same `schema_id()`.

The default implementation returns the same value as
[`schema_name()`](JsonSchema::schema_name).

symbols.name: schema_name
symbols.description:
The name of the generated JSON Schema.

This is used as the title for root schemas, and the key within the root's `definitions`
property for subschemas.

symbols.name: deref
symbols.description:
Dereferences the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be mutably dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref_mut`] concurrently.

symbols.declaration: unsafe fn deref_mut<'a>(ptr: usize) -> &'a mut T;
symbols.description:
Mutably dereferences the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref`] or [`Pointable::deref_mut`]
  concurrently.

symbols.name: drop
symbols.description:
Drops the object pointed to by the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref`] or [`Pointable::deref_mut`]
  concurrently.

symbols.name: inline_schema
symbols.description:
Whether JSON Schemas generated for this type should be included directly in parent schemas,
rather than being re-used where possible using the `$ref` keyword.

For trivial types (such as primitives), this should return `true`. For more complex types,
it should return `false`. For recursive types, this **must** return `false` to prevent
infinite cycles when generating schemas.

By default, this returns `false`.

symbols.name: json_schema
symbols.description:
Generates a JSON Schema for this type.

If the returned schema depends on any [non-inlined](JsonSchema::inline_schema)
schemas, then this method will add them to the [`SchemaGenerator`]'s schema definitions.

This should not return a `$ref` schema.

[`SchemaGenerator`]: https://docs.rs/schemars/1.2.3/schemars/generate/struct.SchemaGenerator.html

symbols.name: schema_id
symbols.description:
Returns a string that uniquely identifies the schema produced by this type.

This does not have to be a human-readable string, and the value will not itself be included
in generated schemas. If two types produce different schemas, then they **must** have
different `schema_id()`s, but two types that produce identical schemas should *ideally*
have the same `schema_id()`.

The default implementation returns the same value as
[`schema_name()`](JsonSchema::schema_name).

symbols.name: schema_name
symbols.description:

This is used as the title for root schemas, and the key within the root's `definitions`
property for subschemas.

- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be mutably dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref_mut`] concurrently.

symbols.name: inline_schema
symbols.description:
Whether JSON Schemas generated for this type should be included directly in parent schemas,
rather than being re-used where possible using the `$ref` keyword.

For trivial types (such as primitives), this should return `true`. For more complex types,
it should return `false`. For recursive types, this **must** return `false` to prevent
infinite cycles when generating schemas.

By default, this returns `false`.

symbols.name: json_schema
symbols.description:
Generates a JSON Schema for this type.

If the returned schema depends on any [non-inlined](JsonSchema::inline_schema)
schemas, then this method will add them to the [`SchemaGenerator`]'s schema definitions.

This should not return a `$ref` schema.

[`SchemaGenerator`]: https://docs.rs/schemars/1.2.3/schemars/generate/struct.SchemaGenerator.html

symbols.name: schema_id
symbols.description:
Returns a string that uniquely identifies the schema produced by this type.

This does not have to be a human-readable string, and the value will not itself be included
in generated schemas. If two types produce different schemas, then they **must** have
different `schema_id()`s, but two types that produce identical schemas should *ideally*
have the same `schema_id()`.

The default implementation returns the same value as
[`schema_name()`](JsonSchema::schema_name).

symbols.name: schema_name
symbols.description:
The name of the generated JSON Schema.

This is used as the title for root schemas, and the key within the root's `definitions`
property for subschemas.

symbols.name: deref
symbols.description:
Dereferences the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be mutably dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref_mut`] concurrently.

symbols.name: deref_mut
symbols.declaration: unsafe fn deref_mut<'a>(ptr: usize) -> &'a mut T;
symbols.description:
Mutably dereferences the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref`] or [`Pointable::deref_mut`]
  concurrently.

symbols.name: drop
symbols.description:
Drops the object pointed to by the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref`] or [`Pointable::deref_mut`]
  concurrently.

symbols.name: inline_schema
symbols.description:
Whether JSON Schemas generated for this type should be included directly in parent schemas,
rather than being re-used where possible using the `$ref` keyword.

For trivial types (such as primitives), this should return `true`. For more complex types,
it should return `false`. For recursive types, this **must** return `false` to prevent
infinite cycles when generating schemas.

By default, this returns `false`.

symbols.name: json_schema
symbols.description:
Generates a JSON Schema for this type.

If the returned schema depends on any [non-inlined](JsonSchema::inline_schema)
schemas, then this method will add them to the [`SchemaGenerator`]'s schema definitions.

This should not return a `$ref` schema.

[`SchemaGenerator`]: https://docs.rs/schemars/1.2.3/schemars/generate/struct.SchemaGenerator.html

symbols.name: schema_id
symbols.description:
Returns a string that uniquely identifies the schema produced by this type.

This does not have to be a human-readable string, and the value will not itself be included
in generated schemas. If two types produce different schemas, then they **must** have
different `schema_id()`s, but two types that produce identical schemas should *ideally*
have the same `schema_id()`.

The default implementation returns the same value as
[`schema_name()`](JsonSchema::schema_name).

symbols.name: schema_name
symbols.description:
The name of the generated JSON Schema.

This is used as the title for root schemas, and the key within the root's `definitions`
property for subschemas.

symbols.name: deref
symbols.description:
Dereferences the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be mutably dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref_mut`] concurrently.

symbols.declaration: unsafe fn deref_mut<'a>(ptr: usize) -> &'a mut T;
symbols.description:
Mutably dereferences the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref`] or [`Pointable::deref_mut`]
  concurrently.

symbols.name: drop
symbols.description:
Drops the object pointed to by the given pointer.

# Safety

- The given `ptr` should have been initialized with [`Pointable::init`].
- `ptr` should not have yet been dropped by [`Pointable::drop`].
- `ptr` should not be dereferenced by [`Pointable::deref`] or [`Pointable::deref_mut`]
  concurrently.

symbols.name: refquill
symbols.description:
Generate a shared JSON API reference from PHP, TypeScript, and Rust.

Analyzers populate [`model::Document`]. The [`artifact`] module validates and
seals the document, and [`wire`] encodes the compact schema-v1 representation.
The command-line interface combines configured inputs and writes one artifact.

symbols.name: artifact
symbols.description: Validate, fingerprint, and atomically write generated API documents.

symbols.name: config
symbols.description: Load and validate source selections and output settings from refquill.json.

symbols.name: model
symbols.description: Complete symbols, types, relationships, and document graph validation.

symbols.name: php
symbols.description: Extract PHP declarations, names, and PHPDoc with Mago.

symbols.name: rust
symbols.description:
Import compiler-generated rustdoc JSON and retain its native metadata.
Compiler-backed Rust API projection. The complete, filtered rustdoc graph is
retained alongside the common symbols, including compiler-specific details.

symbols.name: rust_cargo
symbols.description:
Run Cargo rustdoc for an explicitly configured library or proc-macro crate.
Cargo owns feature selection, macro expansion, cfg and dependency resolution.
Only explicitly configured manifest inputs execute Cargo/build scripts.

symbols.name: typescript
symbols.description: Invoke the bundled TypeDoc and TypeScript compiler worker.

symbols.name: wire
symbols.description:
Encode and decode the compact schema-v1 document and its shared tables.
Version 1 wire contract. Analyzers use the complete semantic model; only this
boundary owns omission, inheritance, type interning, and numeric graph edges.
